transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Gupta (Redwood SE), Liam Torres (Redwood), Ethan Cole (Monsoon CTO), Priya Nair (Monsoon Platform), Rosa Delgado (Monsoon Security)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of org/project key model, quota shapes, and fairness controls in Console/API/Optimize. Focus on multi-tenant guardrails for their telemetry AI product. Agreed pilot next steps and requested benchmarks + security docs.

Topics covered:
- Org vs project key patterns
- Concurrency and token-based quotas
- Priority lanes / burst buffers
- Console demos of routing and sticky keys
- Integration notes for VPC/Private deployment and KMS

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentine's day, hope that's okay, we'll keep this tight. I'm Jordan Park, AE on the account, with Samira and Liam from our infra team.
[00:12] Ethan: Hey Jordan, thanks, excited to dig in — short background, Monsoon runs a multi-tenant telemetry ai offering, heavy embedding use, lots of short-latency calls and some batch jobs.
[00:25] Priya: And we have strict SLA lanes per customer, plus some compliance constraints — we need clear data residency and audit logs.
[00:33] Samira: Great, that's exactly the use-case where org/project key strategy helps. We'll demo the Console first then switch to API patterns and Optimize recommendations.
[00:41] Rosa: Quick ask, we need to know how RBAC and audit entries look for project keys — who can mint keys and see usage.
[00:50] Jordan: Noted, we'll show the SAML SSO and RBAC bit. Okay starting share — sorry if the screen share lags for a sec.
[01:15] Samira: On screen is the Redwood Console, top-level: Organization view. You can create org keys that are global across projects, or scoped project keys.
[01:30] Samira: A common pattern: org-level key for billing and shared infra, project keys for per-customer isolation. You can enforce quotas at either level — e.g., an org quota of 100k tokens/min and per-project slices.
[01:47] Ethan: So project keys are like sub-keys under the org? Does the request still carry org metadata?
[01:52] Samira: Yes the request carries org_id + project_id; routing, quotas, and billing can use either. Slight transcription note: console sometimes shows 'proj id' truncated in the UI — it's just a UI label thing.
[02:10] Liam: Also show fairburst routing — if project exceeds its steady quota, it can consume burst credits from a shared pool if the org policy allows.
[02:25] Priya: We need hard isolation for some enterprise customers — no burst consumption. Can we pin some projects to dedicated capacity?
[02:32] Samira: Absolutely. You can pin a project to Dedicated lanes which are backed by reserved GPU pools. That prevents it using shared org buckets. We can also enforce sticky-routing so requests from a project always go to a particular model family or region.
[02:50] Rosa: How is sensitive request data handled in logs? Do audit logs contain request payloads?
[02:56] Jordan: By default audit logs capture metadata (key, endpoint, token counts, latency); payloads are redacted. For Private deployments there's an option to keep full logs within customer VPC if required, integrated with your KMS/HSM.
[03:15] Ethan: Good. For our SLOs we care about p95 under 250ms for short gen calls. Can you show how concurrency quotas interact with latency?
[03:25] Samira: Sure — concurrency quotas act as backpressure: when concurrency slots are exhausted, requests are queued or get a 429 depending on policy. That prevents overloading backend pools and protects p95. There's a demo policy called 'latency-first' that prioritizes low latency by reserving headroom for steady traffic.
[03:45] Priya: Do you support per-key priority weights? Some of our premium tenants have paid for higher priority.
[03:52] Samira: Yes, priority weights and lanes are supported. You can assign a project weight 0-100; routing will prefer higher-weighted keys and apply fairshare across competitors. There's also preemptive lanes for emergencies.
[04:12] Ethan: How do we enforce token caps? We have both per-minute and daily spend limits.
[04:18] Jordan: In the Console you can set policy rules: rate limit (tokens/second), burst (tokens), daily quota (tokens/day). Alerts and webhook notifications fire when thresholds are hit. We can map limits to billing thresholds as well.
[04:40] Priya: Could we do a mixed model — soft limit that throttles then hard cut at twice the threshold?
[04:46] Samira: Yep, soft then hard is a pattern we call 'grace then deny' — Configure a soft quota that emits warnings and delays, then a hard quota that returns 429. Works well for tiered customers.
[05:03] Ethan: Walk me through how this looks in the API — what's the header footprint?
[05:09] Liam: API requests include Authorization: Bearer <project_key>, X-Redwood-Org: <org_id> and optional X-Project: <project_id>. The runtime uses those headers for routing and quota accounting.
[05:28] Priya: Are project keys rotating automatically? We want short-lived keys for service accounts.
[05:33] Jordan: You can issue ephemeral keys with TTLs, or integrate with your identity provider via SAML/OIDC to mint tokens. We also support key rotation APIs.
[05:50] Rosa: From security review perspective we need KMS for keys, HSM for sensitive workloads, and a full access log. Is that doable in Private?
[05:58] Samira: Yes Private/VPC supports customer-managed KMS and audit retention controls. HSM integrations and FIPS modules are available for enterprise plans.
[06:15] Ethan: About Checkout: we heard you have Optimize recommendations — can Optimize suggest quota configs?
[06:22] Samira: Redwood Optimize analyzes request patterns (seq lengths, tokens per call, embedding sizes), and suggests batching, quantization, and quota shapes. For instance, if embeddings are small and bursty, Optimize will recommend a high-burst buffer with a medium steady-state quota.
[06:40] Priya: Does Optimize auto-apply changes or only recommend?
[06:44] Samira: Recommend only, it can propose a policy bundle which you can preview and apply from Console. We avoid auto applying for obvious safety reasons.
[06:55] Ethan: For the pilot we need a bench: 1k rps sustained for 10 minutes with 128-token responses — can you replicate that?
[07:03] Liam: We can run that in our sandbox against a compatible model, show token cost and p95. We'll need traffic patterns from you — token mix, percent embeddings vs gen.
[07:15] Priya: We'll provide. Also, curious about prefix caching / KV cache — does that affect quota accounting?
[07:22] Samira: Cache hits bypass token generation so they reduce billed tokens but still count towards request quotas unless you explicitly exempt them. There's a distinction between token quota and request quota. We can configure caching rules per route or project.
[07:40] Ethan: So for deduped telemetry requests caching could drop our cost significantly.
[07:44] Samira: Exactly. Optimize will often flag cacheable endpoints and recommend TTLs.
[07:55] Jordan: Quick demo: I'm going to create a policy. Name: 'Monsoon-premium-lane' — set per-project weight 80, daily cap 10M tokens, burst 200k tokens, concurrency 120.
[08:10] [screen shows policy form, some clicks]
[08:20] Samira: Note the policy simulator in Console — you can simulate traffic mixes and see when quotas will be hit. It outputs timeline graphs and expected 429s.
[08:35] Priya: Love the simulator — can it import a HAR file or trace?
[08:39] Samira: You can upload CSV of request traces, HAR import coming soon — internal label says 'har-v1' so it's in early stage.
[08:50] Ethan: About segmentation — do we need separate orgs for different product lines? We have two very different business units.
[08:58] Samira: You can model that as sub-orgs or separate projects within an org. For strict tenancy separation we recommend separate orgs with separate billing and VPCs. For looser separation, project-level scoping works fine.
[09:15] Priya: Any limitations around number of project keys? We have thousands of tenants.
[09:21] Liam: Scales fine, we support hierarchical key catalogs; performance testing with tens of thousands of keys is common. We store lightweight metadata and index by org+project.
[09:33] Rosa: On compliance, will you provide an ATO pack? We need documentation on data flow and encryption in transit + at rest.
[09:40] Jordan: Yes, we'll share our compliance packet and the Private deployment runbook.
[09:50] Ethan: Can you run through a failed-over scenario — if Dedicated pool is saturated what happens?
[09:57] Samira: We have fallback policies: you can set 'deny', 'route-to-shared-with-fallback', or 'route-to-smaller-model'. Many customers choose graceful fallback to a cheaper model family to keep availability.
[10:14] Priya: Would that leak tenant data across pools?
[10:18] Samira: No — routing maintains isolation at the model instance level; if you require cryptographic isolation we recommend Dedicated-only pins or Private deployment.
[10:29] Ethan: About billing, we want cost visibility per project.
[10:34] Jordan: Console shows token-level billing per project, and Optimize has per-route cost breakdowns. You can export CSVs to feed into your FinOps systems.
[10:45] Priya: Are there quotas on the number of policy rules?
[10:49] Liam: No hard limit right now, but we recommend grouping rules for manageability.
[10:57] Ethan: Anything special for embeddings — do you have separate rate limits?
[11:01] Samira: Embeddings are counted by embedding units; you can set separate quotas. We also support batch embedding endpoints to reduce overhead.
[11:14] Rosa: Would batch embedding jobs be scheduled on different pools?
[11:17] Liam: Yes, we can route batch jobs to longer-run GPU instances optimized for throughput.
[11:25] Ethan: On the SDK side, what is the retry behavior on 429s and 503s?
[11:30] Samira: SDKs implement exponential backoff with jitter, and respect Retry-After headers. There's a client-side rate limiter you can opt into to avoid excess retries.
[11:43] Priya: Can we instrument to see per-tenant token consumption in near real-time?
[11:47] Jordan: Yes, streaming telemetry is available — you can subscribe to a topic and get per-key metrics with ~5s granularity.
[11:58] Ethan: Ok great. Let's switch to a mini technical deep dive — Samira, can you show logs of a simulated spike and how policy handled it?
[12:06] Samira: Pulling up a trace — here's a spike where premium tenants started 5x traffic; the policy bumped them into burst pool and non-premium tenants started to see throttles. There's a visual of token burn down and queue lengths.
[12:22] [background voice] Speaker 1: mmm hmm
[12:24] Priya: I see the queue length graph — at 30s we crossed the concurrency threshold. Can we shorten the queue time for premium?
[12:31] Samira: You can decrease max_queue_time for premium projects or reserve concurrency slots. Beware of headroom tradeoffs — too many reserved slots reduces overall throughput.
[12:42] Ethan: Can Optimize recommend a reservation level?
[12:45] Samira: Yes it uses historical traffic to propose reservation percentages to meet p95 targets while maximizing utilization.
[12:55] Priya: Request: can you annotate the policy with stakeholder notes (e.g., contract id, when to escalate)?
[13:01] Jordan: Yep, policies support free-text annotations and links to tickets.
[13:07] Ethan: For the pilot, suggest we do project keys per customer with an org-level shared billing key. We'll pin top 10 enterprise tenants to dedicated lanes.
[13:17] Priya: Agreed. Also need an onboarding script to rotate keys and set up webhook alerts for threshold breaches.
[13:25] Jordan: We'll include a sample script in the handshake pack.
[13:30] Samira: Quick note on k-v cache — sometimes transcriptions show 'KV cash' in docs, weird; but the cache is key-value and stores prefix states to avoid regen. For chat workloads it drastically reduces tokens.
[13:48] Ethan: One more thing: do we have a concept of 'account-level stickiness' so traffic for a tenant goes to same GPU to utilize kv-cache?
[13:55] Liam: Yes sticky routing pins recent keys to the same host for a TTL to exploit KV cache. It's configurable per policy.
[14:06] Priya: For regulatory tenants we need data to never leave eu-west region. How granular is region pinning?
[14:12] Samira: You can pin by org + project to a region; in Private we can restrict to on-prem clusters.
[14:20] Rosa: Please add a note about data egress controls.
[14:23] Jordan: Will do.
[14:29] Ethan: Anything about model quantization affecting latency/accuracy tradeoffs?
[14:33] Samira: Optimize recommends quantization profiles for workloads. It shows expected latency and quality delta. For some LLMs 8-bit quant gets you 2x token throughput with minimal quality loss on classification tasks.
[14:50] Priya: What's the rollback story if a policy causes too many 429s?
[14:54] Samira: Console supports immediate rollback and dry-run prior to apply. Also can route failures to a canary group before global rollout.
[15:05] Ethan: Let's talk timeline — we want pilot next month and production in Q2 if bench looks good. Is that feasible?
[15:12] Jordan: Yes, we'll scope a 4-week pilot: week 0 setup and security review, week 1 benching and config tuning, week 2 live small traffic, week 3 scale and handover.
[15:24] Priya: Who's the Redwood lead for pilot?
[15:27] Jordan: Samira will be lead, Liam will support infra bench runs.
[15:34] Rosa: Security requested an architecture diagram and list of endpoints that will be contacted.
[15:39] Jordan: We'll send network flows and endpoints.
[15:44] [timestamp jumps, later in call] 
[35:10] Samira: We also talked about per-route exemptions — you can mark internal health-check routes as exempt from quota accounting to avoid noise.
[35:22] Ethan: Nice, that helps.
[40:05] Samira: Quick show of API response headers — X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After. SDKs surface these in exceptions.
[40:20] Priya: Can the console generate alerts into PagerDuty for threshold breaches?
[40:24] Liam: Yup, webhook / PagerDuty / Slack integrations exist.
[50:02] Jordan: Wrapping up, key takeaways: project keys per customer, top 10 pinned to Dedicated, use Optimize to tune burst and reservation, provide bench inputs.
[50:18] Priya: We'll give traffic CSV and credentials for a test org.
[50:22] Ethan: Send pilot SOW and pricing examples.
[50:26] Jordan: I will. Samira will run bench.
[50:31] Rosa: Please include SOC2 artifacts and KMS docs.
[50:36] Jordan: On it.
[50:40] [informal chatter about next week's schedules]
[61:55] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and next steps. Bye.
